chunks: "Chew the food for your children with the water of the Euphrates and with the soil of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); if it is not available, then with the water of the sky (rain)."

key_terms.تُرْبَةِ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Soil/Dust of the grave of Al-Husayn
key_terms.حَنِّكُوا: Chew (food) and feed to the newborn

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred substance for chewing food for a newborn in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia practice of *tankeet*, emphasizing the spiritual significance of using water from the Euphrates or soil from Imam Al-Husayn’s grave to connect the newborn to the Ahl al-Bayt. The preference for these specific elements reflects the theological belief in their barakah (blessing), while the allowance of rainwater ensures practical accessibility for the general community.
